content: The provided text is a long list of references and study details, primarily related to infant nutrition, milk consumption, anemia, gastrointestinal blood loss, and related health outcomes. 1. Morley (1999) defined anemia as a hemoglobin concentration below 110 g/L. No specific definition for gastrointestinal blood loss was provided in this study. 2. Fuchs (1993) considered anemia to be present when hemoglobin levels were less than 105 g/L. Gastrointestinal blood loss was not addressed in this study. 3. Thorisdottir (2013) used specific cutoff points for diagnosing iron deficiency anemia (IDA): hemoglobin levels below 105 g/L, mean corpuscular volume (MCV) less than 74 fL, and serum ferritin (SF) levels below 12 µg/L. Gastrointestinal blood loss was not defined. 4. Tunnessen (1987) defined anemia as a hemoglobin concentration below 11 g/dL. No data on gastrointestinal blood loss was provided. 5. Fomon (1981) did not provide a definition for anemia but identified gastrointestinal blood loss through the presence of guaiac-positive stools at 196 days of age. 6. Ziegler (1990) also did not define anemia but identified gastrointestinal blood loss through guaiac-positive stools at 252 days of age. 7. The abbreviation n/a in the table indicates that data or definitions were not available for certain parameters in the respective studies.
